implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's CPS through Promises and async/await, and its contribution is typing the continuation: typing a handler as (value: T) => U makes the result contract explicit where JavaScript leaves it implicit, and typing an async function as Promise<T> forces the caller to await. A hand-written CPS chain typed with generics keeps the answer type visible: Kont<A, R> = (k: (a: A) => R) => R makes a missing continuation a compile error instead of undefined at runtime.
idiom_name: Promise.then / async-await continuations; hand-typed Kont<A, R> = (k: (a: A) => R) => R
pitfalls: Typing a then-callback parameter as any to 'fix' a variance error erases exactly the contract the continuation is meant to express.
An async function returning Promise<void> still requires an await at the call site to sequence it; returning it bare floats the rejection.
Promise.all rejects on the first rejection and leaves the rest running; Promise.allSettled is the type-honest way to observe every continuation.
